ns2:section.sectionText: All other students need department approval. Email ischool-advising@illinois.edu. [Programming for Analytics and Data Processing] Building on the fundamentals introduced in LIS 452, this course adds skills, data structures, tools, and patterns needed for developing and modifying software to solve more complex problems and to improve code maintainability and reliability. These skills are relevant to many types of programming, but many scenarios used will involve data analysis, conversion, validation, and processing pipelines. The course helps prepare students for work on larger projects with multiple developers. Includes test-driven design, more OOP design concepts, refactoring, profiling, introductory parallel processing, and more. Primarily uses the Python language. Prerequisite: LIS452; or equivalent programming knowledge, with consent of instructor.
ns2:section.sectionDeptRestriction: Restricted to students in the Information Sciences department.
